items.title: Fix camera letterboxing and awkward joystick spacing in landscape viewports
items.what: In landscape orientation (Image 9), the 3D dojo viewport is squished into a centered box with black horizontal and vertical letterboxing, while the dual joysticks are pushed to extreme bottom corners separated by a massive black expanse.
items.why: Playing on desktop browsers or landscape mobile devices results in a severely degraded visual presentation and physically uncomfortable control spacing.
items.how: Update camera aspect ratio logic in Three.js to render full-bleed wide viewports on desktop/landscape viewports (`@media (min-aspect-ratio: 1/1)`), floating the HUD elements and joysticks over the 3D canvas with inset corner padding.

items.title: Remove static control legend card covering the lower arena floor
items.what: In active gameplay (Images 3, 4, 5, 10, 13, 15), a large brown card displaying direction bindings ('STANCE / TECHNIQUE') hangs permanently over the tatami mat, directly above joysticks that already repeat 'STANCE' and 'TECHNIQUE' labels beneath them.
items.why: It eats up over 100 pixels of vertical screen real estate on portrait mobile screens, obscuring lower fighter footwork and visually cluttering the combat zone.
items.how: Fade out the helper card after the round timer starts, or move directional icon indicators directly onto the circular joystick base graphic.

items.title: Recolor cyan diamond emblem to match the warm tungsten dojo aesthetic
items.what: The glossy electric blue/cyan 'S$' diamond emblem on the loading screen (Image 1) and gi chest badges (Images 2-5, 8, 10-15) starkly contrasts with the warm golden-brown environment.
items.why: The bright saturated blue badge breaks the dark cinematic 'tungsten and tatami' art direction, looking like an unintegrated placeholder asset.
items.how: Replace the cyan gi badge texture and splash emblem graphics with a warm metallic gold (`#D4AF37`) or brass variant that blends with the UI high-key accents.

items.title: Move active technique text pill closer to fighter action focus
items.what: During technique execution (Images 5 and 13), move name notification pills ('LUNGE PUNCH', 'FRONT KICK') float high in the ambient shoji screen space above the fighters.
items.why: Players must divert their eyes away from the combat point of impact at the center of the frame to check what move was registered.
items.how: Attach the move indicator pill floating directly above the performing fighter's sprite, or integrate it immediately below their respective player name in the top HUD banner.

items.title: Increase color contrast and stroke clarity on opponent red score readout
items.what: In scoring and result screens (Images 8 and 12), opponent point indicators ('1', '2 ½') use a dark muted red text color on a near-black header background.
items.why: The dark red score text falls below basic legibility contrast thresholds, making it difficult for players to quickly read opponent points during fast match resets.
items.how: Brighten the opponent score tint to a saturated coral crimson (`#FF5B5B`) and apply a subtle text glow style matching the golden player score counter.
